issue.title: Correlate GitHub Actions failures with local selection manifests
issue.description: The false-negative metric (find_false_negatives / just selection-health) only correlates local full-lane runs against local scoped-run manifests. CI failures are not fed into the metric at all, so a scoped selection that misses a test which only fails in CI (e.g. a GitHub-runner-only flake or environment difference) is invisible to the metric. This needs the scoped manifest (or its identity) to travel with the change into CI, and a way to pull CI job results back and correlate them the same way local full-lane runs are correlated today. Named in the epic plan's own out-of-scope list. Proposed by epic sase-fp's land phase (sase-fp.8.3), originally proposed during sase-fp.5 (Selection health metrics and false-negative detection).

payload.entry: Backlog triage 2026-08-06 (master 25285417d), closed as one group. The owner asked for the seven highest-impact open tasks and for everything else to be closed with a reason; these nine are the epic sase-fp aftermath that improves an already-working lane rather than fixing broken behavior. Specifically: sase-ft (share the import-graph cache host-locally, ~8.4s once per fresh workspace), sase-fu (re-measure the depth-3 selection table — advisory only, the default is still depth 2), sase-fv (correlate CI failures with local selection manifests), sase-fw (attribute the escalation-rate delta to coverage contexts), sase-fx (coverage-contexts baseline beyond 14-day retention — degradation is graceful, it falls back to the static closure), sase-fz (lazy Pillow import to drop _setup-visual from two lanes), sase-g0 (32s whole-repo collect-only in the contract-manifest test, which now costs the full lane rather than the default scoped one), sase-g1 (a single 'gw22' xdist worker-crash node ID polluting the selection-health store — deletable by hand today), and sase-fg (88s of archive-scale dismissed-bundle setup, which the scoped lane only pays when selected). The one member of this class kept open is sase-g9, because a thin coverage baseline winning on mtime degrades selection ground truth and can therefore make a scoped check pass when it should fail — a correctness problem, not a cost one. Refile any of these individually with fresh measurements if the two-speed lane's cost or accuracy becomes an actual blocker.

payload.close_reason: Backlog triage 2026-08-06: test-selection / test-lane cost, caching, measurement, retention, or metric-hygiene follow-up from epic sase-fp — not a correctness defect. Cut to bring the ready task queue from 30 to 7.
